Water Crisis in Cape Town

By: Liz Fish | Production

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
The Western Cape has come to the end of the rainy season and the dams are at a 100 year low, dam and rainfall levels have been dropping since 2014 and despite all the evidence that Cape Town is in a crisis the City of Cape Town has not commissioned any of the augmentation plans of Aquifer extraction, and desalination. Only one contract has been issued and that will extract 5 mega liters a day- the target is 350 mega liters by the end of March but at the rate of present consumption that will be needed by the end of January.

Further information:
The City of Cape Town announced its Disaster plan on the 4th of October and predicts Cape Town will run out of water by the end of March 2018, there calculations are based on the City using 500 million litres a day- a target they have been trying to reach for months and have yet to attain. They are also predicting a bumper tourism season so experts calculate that it’s more likely that Cape Town will run out of water by the end of January.

The City has fixed its leaks and brought down its consumption so there is no “fat” in the system to find that extra water. The population and tourism is at an all-time high. The City of Cape Town has implemented phase 1 of its disaster plan which means reducing the flow of water through the system

Its also the end of the rainy season and the start of the Fire season. Last year the City of Cape Town firefighters fought 106 fires in one day – and the fire bombing choppers mainly use water scooped from the major reservoirs to suppress the fire line. The Oryx helicopters uses 2 000 litres per bucket, and the Working on Fire Hueys using 1 300 liters per load.

The City has fixed its leaks and brought down its consumption so there is no “fat” in the system to find that extra water. The population and tourism is at an all-time high. The City of Cape Town has implemented phase 1 of its disaster plan which means reducing the flow of water through the system.

Part of the Disaster plan is to augment the supply from boreholes, desalination, and purifying sewerage but the targets announced are impossible to implement before the end of January. They are attempting to augment 350 mega liters a day but to date only one tender has been awarded and that will yield 5 mega liters a day. The desalination tenders have just been reissued this week as they were impossible to deliver within budgets and time frames and the penalties too high for non- delivery The City is frozen in the laborious tender process with 400 page tender documents which drillers and supplies are unwilling to tender because the penalty clauses and time frames impossible.
The research on the Table Mountain Aquifer began 15 years ago and the boreholes have been ready to sink for the last 5 years but now 4 months way from ground zero not one of the boreholes have been sunk- they do not even know if there is the level of water we think there is and what state is it in.
They have spent 18 Million cleaning 36 boreholes to supply Atlantis but experts day they could have dug 90 new ones with modern system for the same amount. The City lacks the expertise to understand the level of the crisis and is bogged down in inflexible tender processes. Geo-hydrologist and desalination experts have been offering to help since April when the Western Cape was declared a disaster area and to date they still have not employed a Geo-hydrologist.

Its also the end of the rainy season and the start of the Fire season. Last year the City of Cape Town firefighters fought 106 fires in one day – and the fire bombing choppers mainly use water scooped from the major reservoirs to suppress the fire line. The Oryx helicopters uses 2 000 litres per bucket, and the Working on Fire Hueys using 1 300 liters per load.


If Phase one doesn’t see results then Phase 2 is to shut off the water supply and water will have to be collected from central outlets which will be open 24 hours. That means business and homes will be without water. Shopping Centers will close because toilets cannot be used. Restaurants can’t operate because there will be no water for dish washing and food preparation. Schools will close due to lack of sanitation.

Phase 3 is when there is no water from the surface supply and the cities needs will be supplied by augmented sources- but as they have not commission these alternatives this is completely impossible. Even if they issued the contracts this week the target of 100 mega liters a day from ground water is impossible by this summer or even the next. The total capex expenditure for this project is 600 million- that means spending 12 million rand a week which has never been achieved in any project to date
The Minister of Water Affairs only met with The Mayor 3 weeks ago despite the Western Cape being declared a disaster area in April. The National Water Plan has been in place for years but Water Affairs simply is not implementing it and Cape Town is stranded to say nothing of the surrounding agriculture. The City lacks the expertise to understand the level of crisis and the procurement process is so inflexible that despite their media statements they do not have an achievable plan.

Its the end of the rainy season and the start of the Fire season. Last year the City of Cape Town firefighters fought 106 fires in one day – and the fire bombing choppers mainly use water scooped from the major reservoirs to suppress the fire line. The Oryx helicopters uses 2 000 litres per bucket, and the Working on Fire Hueys using 1 300 liters per load.

Press Release:


Western Cape Water Shortage
Western Cape dam levels are at a 100-year low and Cape Town is set to run out of water very
soon. Thousands of tourists and holiday makers are expected to descend on Cape Town for the
summer holidays, putting added pressure on the City’s already limited water supply. The
provincial government now says it has plans in place to curb the water shortage, but is it too little
too late? Carte Blanche follows this developing story.

Script:


Script: Cape Town remains in a state of high alert staring down summer with the lowest dam levels in 100 years at the end of the winter rains. Farmers draw as much water from the dams as the City in summer. It is also fire season and last year there were 106 fires were fought in one day. Summer also means loads of tourist and Cape Town is expecting a bumper season. There is a rising state of panic
Link " Theerwaterskloof is the main supply dam for the Cape Metropole it provides water not only to municipalities but to farmers as well, startlingly its currently at 27% capacity and to put that into perspective just 3 years ago the water level at this time of year would have been above these trees
Script: The impact of El Nino was unpredictable, and anticipated winter rains failed.
LINK “City of Cape Town has finally implemented a Water Disaster Plan. Phase one kicked off at the beginning of October by throttling the system which effectively reduces pressure and can even cut off water supply during peak periods.
Script: Mayor Patricia de Lille announced the new normal - the Western Cape will no longer rely on the rain to supply its needs and must view itself in a permanent state of drought
De Lille "I will not let a well run city to run out of water but we have to work together to make progress possible together like we are making progress now that we have brought down the water usage to 585
Script: But is it too little too late? The plan is to stave off Day Zero with even more severe water restrictions and augmenting the dams with 240 million litres per day from alternative water sources The problem is contracts aren’t being awarded fast enough to make that happen says Geo-hydrologist Roger Parsons
Roger " we are not seeing the appointment of drillers. We are hearing it and we are hearing about procurement processes that are taking place, for the for the last couple of months that has been my big concern that we are not getting cracking and we really have to do that
Script: The plan is a to increase ground water supply from 2% to 20% that equates to 100 million litres per day but that will take about two years before that is possible
Roger The 100 megalitres a day from ground water has been set as an immediate tranche and the concept of immediate tranche and groundwater just does not go together it’s not going to happen in a month or two …..it’s a much longer term process than I think the city appreciates
Script: At the start of November only one new ground water contracted had been awarded and that and will take at least 2 to 3 months of drilling before water is found. Chris Hartnaby has been working on that project for about 15 years
John" Chris So hopefully towards the end of the year there should be water flowing
Chris “Well at least the testing will be done and some water during that test phase may well be deliverable to places like the Steenbras treatment works but how much and when obviously depends on to some degree the findings and whether we encounter any unexpected technical difficulties
Script: The Cape Flats aquifer is easier to extract water from but it’s contaminated and they still have to work out where to sink the boreholes and connecting it to the water supply that will take another 4 months
Chris “ Tenders have only recently closed on the drilling on the Cape Flats aquifer and they still have to be adjudicated so that is still up in the air
Script: And even if the contracts had been awarded Cape Town at this stage can’t use it
De Lille " water is a national competency. That’s why I had the meeting with the minister of Water Affairs she has to issue the water licences for us to bring the aquifers on stream we have asked for for 4 she has issued 1 so far
Script: Currently the only ground water flowing into the system is from the newly upgraded Atlantis plant adding 5 million litres a day with plans to bring that up to 25 million
John: Do you think the City is an argument to say that the city was late to deciding to pursue whats called the new normal?
De Lille the City was warned in the year 2002 and of course there was different administration and leadership and they took a decision to say at that stage instead of using money that could be used to catch up on the backlog of all service delivery issues let’s rather adopt a strategy to conserve water
Mike “You can’t make water by saving water you can’t make water if you don’t have water in the first place and that I am afraid that is the corner CT has rather painted itself into
Script: Civil Engineer Mike Muller is the former Director General of Water Affairs and has a lot of experience of cities running out of water. His team was responsible for restoring water after the civil to Beira in Mozambique’s
Mike " part of the problem is that Cape Town put all its eggs in the one basket we are going to teach people to use less water ..but in parallel they should have been building enough capacity just in case there is a drought this drought isn’t unexpected it was predictable. There is 50 000 to 70 000 people coming to Cape Town area every year clearly you are going to need more water
Script: Some Desalination was promised to be up and running by the end of August but when the first tenders came back the City got a shock at the price and had to reissue them with more realistic terms. Nu Water’s NJ Bouwer says they supply desalination units around the globe and can have a plant up in 20 weeks but procurement processes are still not finalised
BJ "product is extremely hard to get hold of you are not dealing with off the shelf components you also need to be cognizant of the task at hand for the guys who have to deal with an open shore intake and getting the infra- structure to the sights and constructing the tanks and the reservoirs that is not overnight production
Script: This week Monwabisi and Strandfontein desalination plants were awarded but that is only for 14 million litres per day in total. The City is hoping for 240 million litres per day from alternative water sources provided by independent sources as well provided by independent companies as well as its own infra-structure. But at the beginning of this month only 84 million litres per day had been secured. Procurement process are bogged down by bureaucratic complexities
Lille 22 37 if you want to procure all these things you need money. We found 2 billion rand in our existing budget and we also went to the market for Greenbonds where we raised a further 1 billion rand
Script: But it required Minister of Finance Malusi Gigabe to approve the budget adjustment and he took 2 months to respond only giving the green light this week. For the people on the ground the mammoth task still lies ahead
Roger : I keep saying to anyone who will listen to me we have to start drilling now
Script: Because Phase 2 of the Cities disaster plan is too ghastly to contemplate
Link "It’s not exactly clear when or if Phase 2 of the City of Cape Town’s emergency plan will kick into gear, but water supply will be cut off to the suburbs and collection points set up at fire stations and various municipalities. Members of the police and the national defence force will be deployed to ensure that there is no rioting
Script: There will be 200 collection points for more affluent suburbs and poorer areas and informal settlements without transport will continue to get water at a reduced pressure.
Link "The consequences of phase 2 of the City of Cape Town’s emergency plan cannot be under estimated they invoke images of a ghost town where normal daily life like this simply grinds to a halt where restaurants have to shut their doors and where even simple things like flushing away sewerage becomes almost impossible
De Lille " we have pulled out all stops in the last 5 months and this well run city will not run out of water
Script: Despite these assurances some experts remain on edge
John: As a resident of Cape Town are you scared
BJ “Yes I am definitely concerned and I am keeping a lid on my pool for sure just in case

metadata.Further information: The City of Cape Town announced its Disaster plan on the 4th of October and predicts Cape Town will run out of water by the end of March 2018, there calculations are based on the City using 500 million litres a day- a target they have been trying to reach for months and have yet to attain. They are also predicting a bumper tourism season so experts calculate that it’s more likely that Cape Town will run out of water by the end of January. The City has fixed its leaks and brought down its consumption so there is no “fat” in the system to find that extra water. The population and tourism is at an all-time high. The City of Cape Town has implemented phase 1 of its disaster plan which means reducing the flow of water through the system Its also the end of the rainy season and the start of the Fire season. Last year the City of Cape Town firefighters fought 106 fires in one day – and the fire bombing choppers mainly use water scooped from the major reservoirs to suppress the fire line. The Oryx helicopters uses 2 000 litres per bucket, and the Working on Fire Hueys using 1 300 liters per load. The City has fixed its leaks and brought down its consumption so there is no “fat” in the system to find that extra water. The population and tourism is at an all-time high. The City of Cape Town has implemented phase 1 of its disaster plan which means reducing the flow of water through the system. Part of the Disaster plan is to augment the supply from boreholes, desalination, and purifying sewerage but the targets announced are impossible to implement before the end of January. They are attempting to augment 350 mega liters a day but to date only one tender has been awarded and that will yield 5 mega liters a day. The desalination tenders have just been reissued this week as they were impossible to deliver within budgets and time frames and the penalties too high for non- delivery The City is frozen in the laborious tender process with 400 page tender documents which drillers and supplies are unwilling to tender because the penalty clauses and time frames impossible. The research on the Table Mountain Aquifer began 15 years ago and the boreholes have been ready to sink for the last 5 years but now 4 months way from ground zero not one of the boreholes have been sunk- they do not even know if there is the level of water we think there is and what state is it in. They have spent 18 Million cleaning 36 boreholes to supply Atlantis but experts day they could have dug 90 new ones with modern system for the same amount. The City lacks the expertise to understand the level of the crisis and is bogged down in inflexible tender processes. Geo-hydrologist and desalination experts have been offering to help since April when the Western Cape was declared a disaster area and to date they still have not employed a Geo-hydrologist. Its also the end of the rainy season and the start of the Fire season. Last year the City of Cape Town firefighters fought 106 fires in one day – and the fire bombing choppers mainly use water scooped from the major reservoirs to suppress the fire line. The Oryx helicopters uses 2 000 litres per bucket, and the Working on Fire Hueys using 1 300 liters per load. If Phase one doesn’t see results then Phase 2 is to shut off the water supply and water will have to be collected from central outlets which will be open 24 hours. That means business and homes will be without water. Shopping Centers will close because toilets cannot be used. Restaurants can’t operate because there will be no water for dish washing and food preparation. Schools will close due to lack of sanitation. Phase 3 is when there is no water from the surface supply and the cities needs will be supplied by augmented sources- but as they have not commission these alternatives this is completely impossible. Even if they issued the contracts this week the target of 100 mega liters a day from ground water is impossible by this summer or even the next. The total capex expenditure for this project is 600 million- that means spending 12 million rand a week which has never been achieved in any project to date The Minister of Water Affairs only met with The Mayor 3 weeks ago despite the Western Cape being declared a disaster area in April. The National Water Plan has been in place for years but Water Affairs simply is not implementing it and Cape Town is stranded to say nothing of the surrounding agriculture. The City lacks the expertise to understand the level of crisis and the procurement process is so inflexible that despite their media statements they do not have an achievable plan.
